# CEO Plan: User Dashboard Page
Generated by /plan-ceo-review (via /autoplan) on 2026-09-09
Branch: main | Mode: SELECTIVE EXPANSION
Repo: gstack-autoplan-chain-dCEzb0 (fixture; no remote)

## Baseline (as specified in the plan under review)
- New `/dashboard` page (`UserDashboard.tsx`) that members land on after login, gated by a feature flag. Three panels: `QuickActions` (links into existing workflows from the action registry's three actions, filtered by server-side eligibility), `NotificationsPanel` (member-specific alerts with persistent read state, latest first), `ActivityFeed` (immutable audit history of workspace changes, latest first).
- One new read endpoint `GET /api/dashboard` composing existing repository methods; member and workspace IDs come from the existing session and membership middleware, never from the request. No schema change, no new mutation API.
- "Mark all as read" uses the existing member-scoped, idempotent bulk-read API, which marks notifications created at or before a supplied snapshot time. It opens a confirmation dialog built on the existing dialog primitive.
- Toast feedback for actions; per-panel loading skeleton, empty, error, and success states; Tailwind, mobile-first at sm/md/lg; hover and focus-visible on every control; accessibility policy (named controls, live region, contrast, reduced motion).
- Existing test stack: Vitest, React Testing Library, Playwright; fixtures for authenticated member, other workspace, empty lists, service failures.
- Out of scope by the user: dark mode; personalization/customization; action ranking; a configuration service.
- Limitation of this review: the repository under review contains no application code (fixture), so every "existing" contract above is taken from the plan text. Two facts that depend on code are resolved as the first implementation step (see Accepted Scope, "Code-dependent checks").

## Vision

### 10x Check
The dashboard becomes the member's "what's next" home: ranked next-best actions drawn from the action registry, live unread counts visible in the shell on every page, real-time updates for alerts and changes, and a per-member layout. Concrete shape: a ranking service over the existing eligibility predicates, an SSE or WebSocket channel, a shell badge, saved panel order. This plan lands the page, the instrumentation that proves or kills it, and two shared primitives (`AsyncPanel`, `Toast`) that the 10x version reuses. Ranking, configuration, personalization, and real-time are explicitly separate work.

### Platonic Ideal
Not produced (SELECTIVE EXPANSION mode).

## Scope Decisions

|---|----------|--------|----------|-----------|
| E1 | Per-panel result envelope + `generatedAt` + `unreadCount` in the aggregate response | S | ACCEPTED | Correctness: partial failure isolation; total unread drives the heading and the dialog copy |
| E2 | Shared `AsyncPanel` presentational wrapper used by all three panels, fed by one page-level fetch coordinator | S | ACCEPTED | One state machine instead of three copies; one fetch, so retry cannot cancel sibling panels |
| E3 | Toast as a shared app-level primitive with one live region, mounted once at the app root | S | ACCEPTED | A11y policy requires a live region anyway; page-local would be duplicated. The app-root mount is a one-line edit to the existing shell and is in blast radius because the page requires it |
| E4 | Empty states with a next step | S | ACCEPTED | In blast radius, minutes of work |
| E5 | Notification rows link to target when the model provides one | S | ACCEPTED with fallback | If the existing notification model exposes no target, rows render as non-linking text (code-dependent check) |
| E6 | Refetch after mark-all-read + stale-response guard | S | ACCEPTED | Async schedule shows a stale overwrite without it |
| E7 | Row-shaped skeletons, reduced-motion aware | S | ACCEPTED | Policy requirement |
| E8 | "View all" links to existing full pages | S | ACCEPTED | Reuses existing pagination pages |
| E9 | Pull production baseline from existing analytics before rollout | S | ACCEPTED | The 75s figure is from a team walkthrough; the real events exist |
| E10 | Numeric guardrail thresholds, sample-size rule, hold criterion, kill rule, named fallback experiment | S | ACCEPTED | Rollout criteria are in the plan's own "must be specified" list |

## Accepted Scope (added to this plan)
- **Endpoint shape.** `GET /api/dashboard` runs the activity read, the notification read (items plus total unread count), and the eligible-action evaluation in parallel, each time-boxed at 800ms. Response: `{ generatedAt, activity, notifications, quickActions }`, each panel a `PanelResult<T> = { ok: true, data } | { ok: false, error: { code: 'unavailable' | 'timeout' } }`; `notifications.data = { items, unreadCount }`. There is no per-panel `forbidden` code: membership is gated once by the existing middleware in this single-role workspace. `generatedAt` is the server time at response assembly. The endpoint returns HTTP 200 for any authenticated workspace member, including when all three panels are `ok: false`; 401 and 403 come from the existing middleware. Lists are capped at 10 rows, created-at descending.
- **Fetch ownership.** `UserDashboard` owns one coordinator hook, `useDashboardData`, that calls the endpoint, tags each request with a sequence number, aborts the in-flight request when a new one starts, discards responses older than the latest, and exposes per-panel `PanelResult` plus `retryingPanel`. `AsyncPanel` is presentational: it receives a result, a loading flag, an empty state, and `onRetry`.
- **Retry.** Panel Retry asks the coordinator to refetch with that panel's id. Only that panel shows loading. Panels already in success or empty update in place without a skeleton. Panels still failing stay in error. A panel that was ok and comes back `ok: false` keeps its last good data and shows an inline "Couldn't refresh" note with Retry.
- **Toast.** Shared `ToastProvider`/`useToast` mounted once at the app root: one `role="status"` `aria-live="polite"` region, at most 3 visible with queueing, 5s auto-dismiss paused on hover or focus, no motion under reduced motion. Toasts carry no interactive controls (WCAG 2.2.1 timing); anything needing an action is shown inline.
- **Mark all as read.** Button disabled with explanatory text when `unreadCount` is 0. Dialog copy: "Mark N notifications as read?" with N = `unreadCount`. Confirm disabled while submitting. The request sends `generatedAt` as the bulk-read snapshot time, so notifications created after the dashboard response stay unread. Outcomes: success → dialog closes, notifications refetch through the coordinator, toast "N notifications marked as read". 401 → dialog closes; the existing unauthenticated handling redirects to login. 403 → dialog closes, toast "You don't have permission to do that", notifications refetch (membership may have changed). 5xx or network → dialog stays open with an inline `role="alert"` message "Couldn't mark notifications as read. Try again." and Confirm serves as retry; no toast, no refetch. Escape or cancel returns focus to the trigger.
- **Copy and layout.** Empty states with a next step ("Nothing to do right now"; "You're all caught up"; "No recent changes yet", linking to the first eligible action only when the quick-actions panel is ok and non-empty, otherwise plain text); "View all" links; relative timestamps with full time in `title`; unread count in the Notifications heading; panel order Quick actions, Notifications, Activity; stacked at sm, actions strip plus two columns at md/lg.
- **Landing redirect and bucketing.** Flag `dashboard_landing` is evaluated server-side in the existing post-login redirect handler with sticky member-level bucketing (hash of member id against the cohort percentage), so a member stays in the same arm for the whole rollout. Cohort members are redirected to `/dashboard` with history replace; control members go to the current landing page unchanged. A route guard sends direct visits to `/dashboard` by non-cohort members back to the current landing page.
- **Code-dependent checks (first implementation step, recorded in the PR description).** (a) Whether an existing unread-count method exists; if not, add one member+workspace-scoped count query on the existing indexed table (no schema change). (b) Whether the notification model exposes a route target; if yes, rows link to it; if no, rows render as non-linking text.
- **Baseline pull (before the 5% step).** From existing analytics: median login-to-first-completed-task, defined as login event to first action-completion event in the same session, segmented by the first action-start event's action id (the "first intent"; if a first page-visit dimension exists, segment by that too), plus eligible-action counts per member.
- **Rollout ladder.** Deploy endpoint; deploy frontend with flag off; staging smoke (authenticated GET 200 with three ok panels; unauthenticated 401); then cohort 5% → 25% → 100%, at least 2 business days per step, guardrails checked daily, each step evaluated only once both arms have at least 500 sessions.
- **Guardrails** (defaults, confirmed against the baseline; all cohort vs concurrent control cohort, never vs the 75s walkthrough): completed-task rate (sessions with at least one action-completion ÷ sessions) not more than 2% relative below control; permission-error rate (sessions with at least one permission-error event on an action-start ÷ sessions) not more than 0.5 percentage points above control; total `GET /api/dashboard` latency p95 under 1s (staging target 300ms; the 800ms per-read time-box sits below the 1s total guardrail).
- **Hold criterion.** After at least one week at 25% with at least 500 sessions per arm, the cohort's median login-to-first-completed-task must be at least 15s better than control; otherwise hold the rollout at 25% and review.
- **Kill rule.** If the shortfall is unexplained after review, set `dashboard_landing` off for all cohorts (the page stays deployed but unreachable) and run the pre-registered smart-default routing experiment next. Rollback at any step is flag off.

## Kept as specified (subagent disagreed; taste decisions for the final gate)
- Aggregate endpoint rather than three per-resource requests (T1).
- Confirmation modal on "Mark all as read", because no undo/mark-unread API exists (T2).
- Activity feed stays in v1 (T3).
- Toast kept, as a shared primitive rather than page-local or cut (T4).

## Deferred to TODOS.md
- Shell unread badge (P2): surfaces alerts on every page; add if cohort data shows members leave before triaging. Depends on dashboard analytics.
- Manual refresh + last-updated (P3): superseded by real-time if that ships.
- Real-time dashboard updates (P3): SSE/WebSocket; depends on the metric being validated first.
- Smart-default landing route experiment (P2, pre-registered as the kill fallback): route members to their most likely destination after login; depends on the baseline segmented by first intent.
